title: Derived completion commutes with tensoring by a finite module or a pseudo-coherent complex
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal in a Noetherian ring A and let ^ denote derived completion with respect to I. The lemma takes K in D^-(A) and asserts two identities: (K tensor^L_A M)^ = K^ tensor^L_A M for a finite A-module M, and (K tensor^L_A L)^ = K^ tensor^L_A L for a pseudo-coherent L in D(A) (source lines 27346-27357). The proof proves (2) and derives (1) as its special case. Represent K by a bounded above complex P^bullet of free A-modules and L by a bounded above complex F^bullet of finite free A-modules (proof lines 27360-27363). Since Tot(P^bullet tensor_A F^bullet) represents K tensor^L_A L, the derived completion (K tensor^L_A L)^ is represented by Tot((P^bullet)^ tensor_A F^bullet), where (P^bullet)^ is the complex whose terms are the ordinary i.e. derived completions (P^n)^, quoting the Noetherian naive-completion proposition and the statement on when derived completion is completion (proof lines 27364-27373). Part (1) is then a special case of (2) (proof line 27374). The non-routine content is the passage from the derived completion of a total complex to the total complex of the completed free resolution: it is what allows the completion to be moved inside the tensor product, at the cost of requiring libreeness of the representing complex and finite freeness of the second factor.
